title: Executable Specification Engine — Capability specification
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods and framings developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. Signature edition. Original Signature methods and framings developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. Executable Specification Engine is a apex creation capability. Purpose: turns formal requirements into implementations and executable acceptance tests.. Inputs: a defined objective with constraints and acceptance criteria. Outputs: the specified artifact — code, design, analysis, or verified result — plus its evidence package. Constraints: available compute, data, tools, and permissions. Expected behavior: the capability either produces a verified result or reports exactly what is missing. Proposed capabilities and research directions — not claims that these already exist or can all be achieved with current technology. 'Boundless' means the catalog and its combinations can keep expanding; actual execution still depends on available compute, storage, data, software, permissions, and physical resources.

function thRun(tests){if(!tests.length)return {total:0,pass:0,fail:[],note:'empty suite'};var pass=0,fail=[];tests.forEach(function(t){try{t.fn();pass++;}catch(e){fail.push({name:t.name,err:String(e.message)});}});return {total:tests.length,pass:pass,fail:fail};}

Verification for executable specification engine: the fragment's own test (demo 3), the limit-enforcement test (demo 4), and the evidence log (demo 5). A capability graduates from 'proposed' to 'verified' only when its tests pass on real inputs, its limits hold under adversarial inputs, and its evidence is recorded. Until then the honest label is 'proposed, fragment verified' — which is exactly what the readiness report (demo 6) states.
